prose_updates.tldr: For independently and uniformly half-randomized populations on two unequal market sides, the optimal covering rectangle at required support \(R\) reduces to a finite residual catalog depending only on \(R\). For \(R\ge4\) and \(n_B,n_S\ge4R\), the exact frontier is the maximum of finitely many affine catalog scores and every tie is retained. On balanced squares, the covering paired-rectangle frontier weakly dominates the published equal-square subclass for every resolution. At \(R=4\), if \(\ell(n)\) is the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, then the published equal-square optimum is exactly \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), while the covering optimum is \(2(n-1)^2+2\). Their exact ratio is \(\ell(n)(1-2/n+2/n^2)\): even sizes form the sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope, whereas prime sizes have ratio \(n-2+2/n\). A constant-incidence sampler implements the selected event, and null-adjusted focal outcomes yield exact one-sided inversion for a sharp constant total effect. No universal collapse of the catalog to diagonal unit residuals is claimed.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact two-sided-market method proves validity for selected equal blocks and treats block choice within that published equal-square subclass; it neither states the general dominance of that subclass by covering paired rectangles nor identifies the support-four optimum \(2n^2/\ell(n)\) from the least nontrivial divisor. General biclique methods establish validity and power guidance but do not classify the optimal covering paired rectangle. Marketplace bias-and-variance analyses motivate the design problem but do not solve this exact rectangle optimization, and existing one-dimensional subset-sum purification does not preserve a prescribed common buyer--seller target fiber.
project_justification.niche: Balanced independent randomization converts admissible covering rectangles into two coupled half-sum profiles. This structure permits an exact finite residual reduction and affine phase analysis for unequal market-side sizes. On balanced squares it contains every published equal-square profile, and at \(R=4\) it yields an exact arithmetic classification of that benchmark through \(\ell(n)\), the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, without asserting an unrestricted-biclique optimum.
project_justification.fill: A two-stage concentration argument bounds the residual on the smaller side and uses a support-preserving residual-copy comparison to bound the larger residual. This yields a finite catalog and an exact affine frontier with all catalog ties. A direct equal-square-profile construction proves dominance over the published equal-square subclass for every resolution. At \(R=4\), every proper equal-block divisor is eligible, so the published equal-square optimum is exactly \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), versus the covering paired-rectangle value \(2(n-1)^2+2\). The exact ratio \(\ell(n)(1-2/n+2/n^2)\) has its sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope on even sizes and equals \(n-2+2/n\) at prime sizes. The same catalog supports an implementable conditional law and exact one-sided sharp-null inversion. Whether every catalog entry can be purified to a dominating diagonal unit-residual entry remains a separate open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026) establish the equal \(k\)-block total-effect test and motivate the support--focal-size trade-off. The covering paired-rectangle class contains their published equal-square profiles, which gives weak dominance at every resolution. At support four, the present result proves the exact published-subclass optimum \(\Phi_n^{\mathrm{eq}}(4)=2n^2/\ell(n)\), with \(\ell(n)\) the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, and compares it with the exact covering paired-rectangle optimum \(2(n-1)^2+2\). Even sizes give the sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope, while prime sizes give ratio \(n-2+2/n\). Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022) encode imputable tests as bicliques and motivate large bicliques, but do not supply the paired-rectangle classification. Li, Zhao, Johari, and Weintraub (2021) study interference-induced bias and variance in two-sided marketplace experiments, and Johari, Li, Liskovich, and Weintraub (2022) analyze bias under two-sided platform designs; both motivate why focal retention and design choice matter, but neither is a competing exact covering-rectangle optimization result. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) provide the conditioning-mechanism validity theorem used after imputability is verified. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024) provide the orbit-equivariance template, while unequal rectangular profiles require a separate constant-incidence count. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021) provide discrete Fisher inversion machinery, specialized here after null-adjusted dyadic imputability and crossing monotonicity are established. Singhal (2019) motivates bilinear subset-sum profiles and one-dimensional purification, but does not furnish a coupled common-fiber-preserving reduction to diagonal unit residuals. Ye et al. (2023) provide the unequal-side marketplace consumer through Platform O's independent user-view and ad randomizations.
prose_updates.interpretation: The finite-catalog result is the actionable design certificate: for fixed resolution \(R\), one enumerates \(\mathcal C_R\), evaluates the affine scores at the two market sizes, and retains every maximizer on a phase boundary. On balanced squares, this covering design class weakly dominates the published equal-square subclass at every resolution by reproducing each eligible equal-square profile. The \(R=4\) slice has a complete arithmetic comparator: letting \(\ell(n)\) be the least divisor of \(n\) at least two, the best published equal-square profile retains \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), while the optimal covering paired rectangle retains \(2(n-1)^2+2\). The exact ratio is \(\ell(n)(1-2/n+2/n^2)\). Even sizes, for which \(\ell(n)=2\), attain the sharp lower envelope \(2-4/n+4/n^2\) and establish limit inferior two; prime sizes, for which \(\ell(n)=n\), have ratio \(n-2+2/n\) and therefore a linear-scale separation. These comparisons concern the published equal-square subclass, not unrestricted bicliques. The unresolved unit-residual question concerns only whether the already finite computation admits a further universal closed-form collapse; it is not needed for catalog optimality, this exact comparison, sampling, or exact one-sided inversion.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves the finite residual catalog, exact affine frontier and catalog equality cases, the constant-incidence sampler, and exact one-sided inversion under the sharp constant total-effect null. On balanced squares, it proves that covering paired rectangles weakly dominate the published equal-square subclass for every resolution. At \(R=4\), it also proves the exact published equal-square comparator formula \(2n^2/\ell(n)\), the exact gap and ratio against the covering paired-rectangle optimum, the sharp even-size factor-two asymptotic lower envelope, and the prime-size ratio \(n-2+2/n\). Universal unit-residual purification remains an explicit unresolved question and is not used by those results. The note makes no claim about weak-null validity, power or confidence-width optimality, unrestricted bicliques, minimality of the \(4R\) threshold, ordinary two-sided \(95\)-percent inversion at support \(20\), or the empirical validity of the constant-effect exposure model for Platform O.
